basis: Brain malformations, epilepsy and severe developmental impairment define disease; strabismus affects 3/5 (60%); optic nerve hypoplasia is occasional.
Keratin-filled cyst arising from the hair follicle outer root sheath.
Immune dysregulation with immunodeficiency, severe infantile bowel inflammation and defining arthritis; lymphoma is a later risk.
Limb dysplasia, camptodactyly and cleft palate define syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%; skin dimples do not establish skin damage.
Defined renal pain disorder with possible hematuria; pain alone does not establish neurologic injury.
Widespread cutaneous keratoacanthomas; structural eyelid involvement with ectropion in 30-79%; corneal disease and dysphagia occur in only 5-29%.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; cleft palate in 7/11 (64%); contractures in 6/11 (55%), clubfoot in 5/11 and scoliosis in 4/11.
Polyp confined to the vulva, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Carcinoma arising in breast tissue; breast has no axis. Metastatic sites are not intrinsic organ labels.
Progressive corticospinal disease; scoliosis and pes cavus are each annotated at 30-79%, although described qualitatively as less common.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and movement disorder; esotropia in 3/7 (43%); reflux in 4/7 does not establish direct gastrointestinal injury.
Defective alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation causes muscular dystrophy; brain and eye disease vary substantially across subtypes and are not established for most patients.
Neoplasm originating in breast parenchyma; breast is outside the axes.
Mitochondrial lactic acidosis and sideroblastic anemia; liver dysfunction and cardiac defects/AV block in 1/1 reported patient; seizures omitted under four-axis cap.
Cardiomyopathy, muscle weakness and thrombocytopenia each affect 2/2; elevated CK supports myopathy. Alopecia totalis in 2/2 omitted under four-axis cap.
Severe brain malformations and metacarpal dysplasia define syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 80-99%.
Rhodesian sleeping sickness commonly progresses to direct CNS invasion and meningoencephalitis (>30% over untreated course); blood parasitemia alone is not blood-cell damage.
Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid-cell malignancy; lymphoma also requires the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
Dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; abnormal muscle contractions do not establish primary skeletal muscle disease.
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes define MELAS; sensorineural hearing loss affects roughly 50-60%; MTTS1-specific estimates are limited.
Usually phenotypically silent with no intrinsic organ dysfunction; recessive diseases unmasked by homozygosity are separate diagnoses.
Intestinal atresia and volvulus with absent mesentery define gastrointestinal disease; absence of the superior mesenteric artery is a defining vascular malformation.
Pathologic involuntary speech repetition is a disorder of neurologic language and communication function; no additional organ injury is inherent.
Inherited lipoate synthesis disorder; direct encephalopathy, seizures or progressive motor-system disease occur in most presentations (>50%); other organ injury varies by subtype.
Clostridial bacterial infection; neurologic, intestinal and soft-tissue injury depend on species and syndrome, with no additional organ established across most of this umbrella.
